packages.label: אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה וְטַעֲמָהּ
packages.label_en: The Light and Taste of Torah
packages.reason: These concepts all express the same essential quality: the enduring, self-sustaining illumination that the Tzaddik's Torah imprints in a person. טַעַם הַתּוֹרָה (tasting the Torah), אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה (the light of Torah), and נֵר (the candle that does not go out) are all bechinas of the same reality — a spiritual contact with holy teaching that, once experienced, permanently illuminates even in absence. The Tzaddik's Torah (תּוֹרַת הַצַּדִּיק) and his 'merchandise' (סְחוֹרָה) are two ways of naming the same object of that contact.

packages.label: הִתְרַחֲקוּת וְלַיְלָה
packages.reason: The Torah explicitly states two bechina equations that bind these nodes together: (1) הִתְרַחֲקוּת (distancing from the Tzaddik) IS a bechina of לַיְלָה (night), and (2) לַיְלָה and חֹשֶׁךְ (darkness) are paired as equivalent states — 'בְּחִינַת לַיְלָה וְחֹשֶׁךְ'. All three concepts express the same negative existential state: the condition of being spiritually cut off from the source of light. They are not cause-and-effect (distancing does not produce night; it IS night). This is the evil mirror of Package 1: where Package 1 is the persistent light, Package 2 is the darkness that light penetrates.
